messages:
rachel: seeing unexpected provisional tokens attributed to route 'cheap-eu' even though the confirmed charges land on 'stable-eu' after router reroute. any ideas?

ben: paste an example trace? looks like an affinity flip during a reconnect might be creating provisional rows on the incoming route before sticky routing finishes.

rachel: snippet from a customer session:
```
[2026-07-03T10:22:11Z] router recv session=foo SNI=app.example route=cheap-eu provisional=2
[2026-07-03T10:22:12Z] router reroute session=foo -> stable-eu confirmed=18
```

ops-bot: created alert: PROV-ROUTE-MISMATCH-451

ben: hmm if provisional uses the initial route tag but confirmed uses final route we get split visibility in console and billing. ledger should record both route_of_record and route_final to reconcile.

rachel: agreed. console currently aggregates provisional/confirmed by route tag and that makes it look like cheap-eu is leaking credits.

billing: if provisional ends up attributed to different route customers could dispute invoices. we need a clean reconciliation column.

ux-team: from UX: propose a "route lineage" column in the provisional table and a toggle to rollup by initial vs final route. will help ops and billing trace anomalies.

ben: implementation plan: (1) router to emit x-route-origin header at first connection (2) backend to include both origin_route and final_route in provisional rows (string tags) (3) ledger schema add two string fields (we can keep them as tags) and console to surface route-lineage.

rachel: also will help with quota enforcement. current per-route quota check uses final_route only and provisional charging on origin route can exceed per-route soft cap. we should check quota against union(origin, final) or against origin for provisional and final for confirmed.

ben: my vote: evaluate provisional against origin_route quotas to avoid early overcommit, and confirmed against final_route quotas. add a safety cap that if provisional+confirmed across both routes exceeds global hard limit, we reject.

billing: please also emit an "attribution_reason" tag (e.g., reroute, canary-swap, affinity-loss) so refunds can be grouped. need CSV export for accounting.

ops-bot: ticket INFRA-1301 created for headers/ledger, CON-879 for console lineage tiles, BILL-512 for export.

rachel: QA: simulate sticky session loss -> reroute during streaming with mixed small recon and big confirms. expect provisional->confirmed lineage map and verify quotas not breached for any route.

ben: rollout: behind FF for 2 weeks, console tile beta for SREs, billing review before auto-refunds enabled.

ux-team: we'll prototype the lineage UI and mock data; keep it minimal: table + Sankey showing origin->final counts.

rachel: thanks all. this should stop the misleading per-route provisional spikes. follow-ups in INFRA-1301, CON-879, BILL-512.
